notes.short: Dark as Kedar's tents, lovely as Solomon's curtains
notes.about: The verse names two things, then two likenesses, in turn. The tents of Kedar answer to dark, and the curtains of Solomon to lovely.
notes.evidence: Lowth says the last line is to be divided and its parts applied separately to what goes before. Kingsbury, in Barnes' Notes, and Fausset (Jamieson, Fausset and Brown) read dark as the tents of Kedar and lovely as the curtains of Solomon.

cites.quote: The last line here is also to be divided and separately applied to the preceding
cites.read: the 1816 printing, in the scan at archive.org/details/lecturesonsacred02lowt

cites.quote: Dark-hued, as the tents of Kedar with their black goats' hair coverings, rough and weather-stained ... but comely (beautiful) as the rich hangings which adorn the pavilion of Solomon.

cites.quote: black--namely, "as the tents of Kedar," equivalent to blackness ... To feel this, and yet also feel one's self in Jesus Christ "comely as the curtains of Solomon," marks the believer
